model_annotation: The bar chart compares the percentage shares of Aluminium, Kupfer (Copper), and Nickel in Germany and the EU for the years 2021, 2022, and 2023. In Germany, Nickel consistently holds the largest share, decreasing slightly from 25.1% in 2021 to 24.7% in 2022 and then to 11.4% in 2023; Kupfer follows with values of 8.3%, 11.3%, and 2.2% respectively; and Aluminium shows the smallest shares at 3.6%, 2.7%, and 1.0%. In the EU, Nickel also dominates, with shares of 24.3% in 2021, 23.3% in 2022, and 14.6% in 2023; Kupfer increases from 4.4% to 5.1% before dropping to 1.3%; and Aluminium declines from 3.2% to 2.8% to 1.7%. Each category is represented by three adjacent bars—blue for 2021, purple for 2022, and gray for 2023—with exact percentage values labeled atop each bar. The vertical axis is scaled from 0% to 30% in increments of 5%, and the horizontal axis lists the three metals under each regional heading (“Deutschland” and “EU”). The chart visually highlights the dominance of Nickel in both regions and the general downward trend across all metals from 2021 to 2023, particularly sharp for Nickel in Germany in 2023.
